text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALE - Two Philippine firms bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for March shipment, Manila grains traders said.

OILSEED SALE - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation bought 10,000 tonnes of palm kernel meal at $98 a tonne, C and F. The NLCF passed on tenders for 10,000 tonnes of ricebran and 20,000 tonnes of copra because offer prices were too high, a NLCF official said.

SOYOIL SALE - USDA said net soybean oil sales to China in the week ended February 13 totalled 23,000 tonnes. In its weekly export sales report, USDA said the China activity included 2,000 tonnes in new sales and 21,000 tonnes in destination changes.

WHEAT TENDER - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association would tender on Thursday for two shipments totalling 69,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, Taipei traders said. The first shipment would be slated for March 15 to April 5 delivery from the Pacific Northwest. The second shipment would be slated for March 31 to April 20 from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - The European Union will hold a tender on February 25 to supply 45,000 tonnes of EU soft wheat as food aid to Bangladesh, France's grain office ONIC said. The EU will hold another tender on the same day to supply Ivory Coast with 2,480 tonnes of EU maize flour as food aid, it said.

- The CCC said it seeks a total of 10,530 tonnes U.S. hard red wheat under its export program to Bangladesh. The wheat was divided into two offers. One was for 5,870 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat and the other was for 4,660 tonnes HRW or hard red spring wheat. Shipment period for both was for March 15-April 10. Offers were due February 26.

SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan BSPA's Taichung Division will retender for one 54,000 tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans at a tender on Tuesday, traders said on Friday. The BSPA Taichung Division passed on the tender on Friday.
CORN TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of 18,000 tonnes of maize, with shipment in March 1997. Tenders close on February 25, the commission said.

CORN, RICE, CORN/SOY BLEND TENDER - The Commodity Credit Corp of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it was seeking a total of 32,380 tonnes U.S. corn, rice and corn/soy blend for shipment to North Korea. The deal included 5,000 tonnes of corn-soy blend, 20,780 tonnes of yellow corn and 6,600 tonnes milled rice. Delivery at port was slated before April 1. Offers were due on February 25.
MARKET TALK - Brazil traders said they had heard talk that China resold up to 400,000 tonnes of South American soymeal but they had no confirmation as yet.
